title: Ship does not set ticket done in 0.6.1 for a run started on a ticket
body: What happened: after warden done at the ship step (PG-330, flow feature), the ticket file still said status: todo on main. The 0.6.1 upgrade note says a run started with --ticket gets its ticket set to done by warden at ship. Expected: status done, committed with the run record. Steps: upgrade 0.6.0 to 0.6.1, run a ticket to ship, merge, run warden done, read the ticket file. Evidence: warden done returned status shipped; grep ^status backlog/PG-330.md printed status: todo; I had to run warden tools tickets set-status PG-330 done by hand. Unsure whether the run was started with --ticket.
note: Not a warden fault. The ticket is only set to done at ship when the run was started with the ticket flag. Your run files show it was not, so the ticket was left alone. Start the run with the ticket flag, or set it by hand.

thread.text: Was the PG-330 run started with --ticket? Please look at the run's events for a ticket.status entry (or ticketError in the run file) and tell us what it says.

Looks like the run was not started with --ticket, but I can't prove it. There is no ticket.status event and no ticketError anywhere in .warden (state/PG-330 and history/PG-330 events.jsonl and run.json, plus a search of all of .warden). The run.started event only has flow, branch, worktree and baseSha, and run.json has no ticket field. The run's task name is PG-330 and task.md starts with '# PG-330: <title>', but nothing records a ticket link. Event types present: run.started, step.*, session.linked, output.accepted, gate.*, check, review, review.round, route.back, proof.stale, stop.blocked, ship, history.written. I did not read the ticket file or the exact start command; the start command is not logged.
